source_table: Clinical Safety Review sec 8.5.1 'Uninterpretable platelet counts due to platelet clumping' (PDF p165)
notes_measurement: Study CS2: 26 of 112 (23%) inotersen subjects had at least 1 clumped platelet sample vs 8 of 60 (13%) placebo. Mechanism proposed: reaction between antiplatelet antibodies and EDTA. Clinically material - in 2 of the 3 severe <25 x10^9/L cases (one fatal) clumped samples delayed diagnosis and treatment. Graded 1: analytical interference, not itself a platelet count reduction.

source_table: Clinical Safety Review sec 8.5.1 (PDF p162) and Table 35 (PDF p163), cols 'Number of Reduced Doses after First Dose Pause' / 'Reduced Dose Regimen'
notes_measurement: REDUCED-DOSE BAND ROW. Of the 27 subjects who paused for platelets <75 x10^9/L: 18 resumed the full 300 mg weekly dose, of whom 6 could not maintain full dosing (received <10 full doses); 12 received reduced regimens, 'usually approximately half the full inotersen dose (150-160 mg) every week'. Regimens printed in Table 35 include 160 mg/week, 150 mg/week, 150 mg every 2 weeks, 160 mg every 2 weeks, and 80 mg/week or 80 mg every 2 weeks in one subject. Reviewer comment: 'The efficacy of these reduced doses has not been established in clinical studies.'

source_table: Combined Clinical/Biostatistical Review sec 4.4 'Nonclinical Pharmacology/Toxicology' (PDF p17)
notes_measurement: CROSS-SPECIES EXPOSURE-MARGIN row. Verbatim: 'Safety margins based on AUCs at the no observed adverse effect levels (NOAELs) for severe thrombocytopenia in monkeys and kidney toxicity in rats were <= ~2-fold, suggesting monitoring in humans may be warranted.' Graded 3 because the severe (fatal-in-animals) thrombocytopenia NOAEL sits at or below ~2x the human clinical AUC - i.e. the severe effect occurs at essentially clinical exposure, which is the animal analogue of the rubric's grade-3 'at or below therapeutic plasma concentration' criterion. Human reference exposure: Cmax 12.1 ug/mL at 300 mg SC weekly.

notes_measurement: IMPORTANT CAVEAT - this is an absence-of-listing, not an explicitly reported zero. notes_measurement: Graded 2 (moderate) rather than 3 because the abstract does not give a platelet count or a severity band - only 'acute dose-dependent thrombocytopenia'. Mechanism: TLR9- and Syk-dependent, IVIg-rescuable, with raised plasma MCP-1; CpG ODN also activated human platelets in vitro and drove Syk-dependent phagocytosis by THP-1 monocytes.
